channel.title: Pier & Point · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: No source read names an architect for the towers' shell
item.description: No source read names an architect for the towers' shell; the SHoP Architects page on ArchDaily covers the campus's other two buildings. In May 2023 the SF Standard reported Uber marketing 1725 3rd St for sublease and described it as never occupied by Uber; an Uber spokesperson said only that one of its buildings was unoccupied. Source: https://www.archdaily.com/1006339/uber-headquarters-shop-architects ; https://sfstandard.com/2023/05/18/uber-looks-to-sublease-fully-furnished-san-francisco-office-it-never-occupied/ ; https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2025/02/14/warriors-uber-alexandria-bag-500m-loan-for-office-complex/.

item.title: Correction · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: The Uber 3 & 4 page now shows that February 2025 press…
item.description: The Uber 3 & 4 page now shows that February 2025 press reports disagree on who leases the offices (The Real Deal: Uber and the Warriors each lease office space; Commercial Observer: both buildings are 100 percent leased to Uber). The 2021 completion date now rests on the SF Standard alone; Office Snapshots shows 'Year 2020' without saying what it means. Source: The Real Deal, 2025-02-14 (therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2025/02/14/warriors-uber-alexandria-bag-500m-loan-for-office-complex/); Commercial Observer, 2025-02-11; Office Snapshots, 2022-01-24.

item.title: Correction · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: The Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 page now notes that Uber's own…
item.description: The Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 page now notes that Uber's own annual reports may give a different completion year than SF Standard's 2021, and that they could not be opened. Source: Uber Technologies Form 10-K (sec.gov; not readable on 2026-10-12); SF Standard, 2023-05-18; Office Snapshots, 2022-01-24.

item.title: Correction · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: The SHoP Architects credit on ArchDaily is for Uber's…
item.description: The SHoP Architects credit on ArchDaily is for Uber's buildings at 1455 and 1515 Third St, not 1655 and 1725, so it is not shown for these towers; Huntsman Architectural Group is credited for their interiors. Office Snapshots calls both towers eleven stories and LEED v4 Gold; OpenStreetMap tags 1655 Third St at twelve. Completion is 2021 per SF Standard, while Office Snapshots lists 'Year 2020' without saying what it means. A 2017 Mortenson item is about the start of arena steel; it does not date the office towers' construction. Source: ArchDaily (archdaily.com/1006339/uber-headquarters-shop-architects); Office Snapshots, 2022-01-24; SF Standard, 2023-05-18; Mortenson, 2017-11-20 (mortenson.com/news-insights/chase-center-structural-steel).

item.title: Correction · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: Two 2018 steel-erection entries for Uber's office towers were…
item.description: Two 2018 steel-erection entries for Uber's office towers were schedule forecasts shown as events. They are now one entry dated to Mortenson's November 2017 report that steel work had begun. Source: https://mortenson.com/news-insights/chase-center-structural-steel.

item.title: Correction · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: The record no longer says Uber has occupied both towers since…
item.description: The record no longer says Uber has occupied both towers since January 2022 on a 20-year lease for about 4,000 employees, or that it leases the entire office component: The Real Deal (2025) says Uber and the Warriors each lease office space there, and SF Standard (2023) says Uber never occupied 1725 Third St and was marketing it for sublease. SHoP Architects is now cited to ArchDaily (with Huntsman credited for the interiors by Office Snapshots), the joint venture to The Real Deal, LEED v4 Gold to Office Snapshots, and completion to 2021 (SF Standard, Office Snapshots) instead of June 2021. The steel-erection dates are now labelled as Mortenson's November 2017 schedule rather than recorded events, and the Alexandria supplemental is dated January 2018, when it was filed. The note that Uber 'never fully staffed' 1725 Third St now says 'never occupied', as SF Standard does. Source: The Real Deal, 2025-02-14 (https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2025/02/14/warriors-uber-alexandria-bag-500m-loan-for-office-complex/); The San Francisco Standard, 2023-05-18 (https://sfstandard.com/2023/05/18/uber-looks-to-sublease-fully-furnished-san-francisco-office-it-never-occupied/); ArchDaily, 2023-09-04 (https://www.archdaily.com/1006339/uber-headquarters-shop-architects); Office Snapshots, 2022-01-24 (https://officesnapshots.com/2022/01/24/uber-mission-bay-headquarters-san-francisco/); Mortenson, Chase Center structural steel, 2017-11-20 (https://mortenson.com/news-insights/chase-center-structural-steel); Alexandria Real Estate Equities Q4 2017 supplemental, SEC (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001035443/000103544318000022/a4q17ex991supp.htm).

item.title: Milestone · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: SF Standard reports that Uber is marketing the… (May 18, 2023)
item.description: SF Standard reports that Uber is marketing the entirety of 1725 Third St for sublease and that the building was never occupied by Uber; an Uber spokesperson says one of its four Mission Bay buildings is currently unoccupied (May 18, 2023). Source: The San Francisco Standard, 2023-05-18.

item.title: Complete · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: Both towers complete construction (SF Standard: the… (~2021)
item.description: Both towers complete construction (SF Standard: the four-building campus was initially completed during the pandemic in 2021; no month is sourced) (~2021). Source: The San Francisco Standard, 2023-05-18.

item.title: Complete · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (1655 & 1725 3rd St) completed… (~2021)
item.description: Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (1655 & 1725 3rd St) completed in 2021 per SF Standard (May 18, 2023: the four-building campus was 'initially completed during the pandemic in 2021'; that article gives the year only for 1725 3rd St); Office Snapshots (Jan 24, 2022) lists 'Year 2020' without saying what the year means (~2021). Source: https://sfstandard.com/2023/05/18/uber-looks-to-sublease-fully-furnished-san-francisco-office-it-never-occupied/; https://officesnapshots.com/2022/01/24/uber-mission-bay-headquarters-san-francisco/.

item.title: Milestone · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: Alexandria Real Estate's Q4 2017 earnings… (~Jan 2018)
item.description: Alexandria Real Estate's Q4 2017 earnings supplemental discloses a joint venture with Uber and the Golden State Warriors "expected to be formed in February 2018" for "two office buildings aggregating 580,000 RSF, adjacent to the Golden State Warriors arena, which are 100% leased to Uber," with Alexandria's $31.0 million initial equity contribution representing a 10% interest (~Jan 2018). Source: Alexandria Real Estate Equities Q4 2017 supplemental (SEC filing, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001035443/000103544318000022/a4q17ex991supp.htm).
item.source: Alexandria Real Estate Equities Q4 2017 supplemental (SEC filing, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001035443/000103544318000022/a4q17ex991supp.htm)

item.title: Milestone · Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4: Mortenson's news item of 11/20/2017… (Nov 20, 2017)
item.description: Mortenson's news item of 11/20/2017 (publication date) reports structural steel work starting on the Chase Center development, which includes two office buildings (the page gives no street addresses; Pier & Point reads them as 1655 & 1725 3rd St). The 11/20/17 start is for the arena; the item's schedule has office-building steel running 2/27/2018 to 8/18/2018 and the project's 'topping out' (completion of all structural steel) on 9/1/2018 – 6,000 tons of office-tower steel, fabricated by Gayle Manufacturing Co. and erected by Cal Erectors. The item is a schedule, and no report of the actual office-steel dates was read, so it does not date when the office towers went under construction (Nov 20, 2017). Source: https://mortenson.com/news-insights/chase-center-structural-steel.
